sections.title: The Inheritance of the Promise
observations: In this section, Paul contrasts the status of believers as heirs of God's promise with that of slaves. He emphasizes that before faith in Christ, we were like children under guardians, but now, through Christ, we have received the Spirit and are adopted as sons and daughters of God.

Paul uses the analogy of an heir who, although he is the owner of everything, is treated like a slave until he comes of age. This illustrates the transition from the law to grace, where believers are no longer under the law but are now children of God.

sections.title: The Danger of Turning Back
observations: Paul expresses concern for the Galatians, warning them against returning to their former ways of legalism and bondage. He reminds them of their past experiences and the joy they had in receiving the gospel.

This section highlights the emotional appeal Paul makes, as he refers to the Galatians as his children and expresses his anguish over their spiritual state. He fears that his labor among them may have been in vain.

sections.title: The Allegory of Hagar and Sarah
observations: In this section, Paul uses the story of Hagar and Sarah to illustrate the two covenants: the covenant of law represented by Hagar and the covenant of promise represented by Sarah. He argues that those who rely on the law are like children of Hagar, while those who trust in God's promise are like children of Sarah.
This allegory serves to reinforce the idea that believers are free and should not submit to the yoke of slavery that comes from legalism.

importantVerses.commentary: But when the fullness of time had come, God sent forth his Son, born of woman, born under the law, to redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive adoption as sons.
My little children, for whom I am again in the anguish of childbirth until Christ is formed in you!

questions: What does it mean to be adopted as sons and daughters of God?
How does the allegory of Hagar and Sarah apply to our understanding of the law and grace?
In what ways can we be tempted to return to a legalistic mindset after experiencing grace?
